title: Kashima — 鹿嶋
goal: Say where you stand/wait and distinguish verb patterns from place-name readings.

blocks.text: The current city name is **鹿嶋市**. The well-known shrine's name is **鹿島神宮**; its spelling uses 島. We preserve the official words rather than silently standardising every label to one island character.
**鹿嶋で友だちに会います。** かしまで ともだちに あいます。 — I meet my friend in Kashima.
Today's language is ordinary waiting and standing in a fictional meeting scene. Knowing shrine history is not required to answer the Japanese test.

cards.title: Inside 鹿嶋, and related 鹿島

items: **Character:** 鹿 · **Meaning/reading:** deer; か here, ordinary しか · **Radical/components:** 鹿, しか; whole deer-derived form, modern 广-like top and 比-like lower shapes · **Status:** Encounter; its indexing radical is 鹿, not 广.
**Character:** 嶋 · **Meaning/reading:** island; しま · **Radical/components:** 山, やまへん, beside 鳥 · **Status:** Encounter.
**Character:** 島 · **Meaning/reading:** island; しま · **Radical/components:** 山 inside/below an abbreviated bird-related upper shape · **Status:** Encounter review from 松島/福島.

blocks.text: **鹿嶋 / かしま; 鹿島神宮 / かしまじんぐう.** The variant shapes explain the reading connection; they do not authorise changing an official city's spelling. 神/宮 stay helped within the shrine word.
**立つ / たつ — stand; 立ちます / たちます.** 立 is its own radical, たつ; learn the whole standing-person-derived shape. The name 日立 used an encountered たち; now a useful action gives 立 formal study.
**駅の前に立ちます。** えきの まえに たちます。 — I stand in front of the station.
With this position model に identifies the standing location. **立ちません / たちません; 立ちました / たちました; 立ちませんでした / たちませんでした.** The polite stem is 立ち, not 立つ＋ます. Broader te-form formation comes in Gunma.
**待つ / まつ — wait; 待ちます / まちます.** 待 has radical 彳, ぎょうにんべん, with 寺 as a historical sound component. 彳 has a walking/movement association; its three strokes differ from 亻, the person radical in 休.
**友だちを待ちます。** ともだちを まちます。 — I wait for my friend.
**駅で待ちます。** えきで まちます。 — I wait at the station.
The person/thing awaited takes を; the waiting activity's place takes で. English “for my friend” does not automatically mean Japanese に after 友だち.

cards.title: Stand at a position; wait at an activity place

blocks.text: **駅の前に立ちます。** えきの まえに たちます。 — I stand in front of the station.
**駅の前で友だちを待ちます。** えきの まえで ともだちを まちます。 — I wait for my friend in front of the station.

Both sentences can describe the same scene while relating the place differently to the verb. Do not make a universal rule that “all action verbs take で” or “all places take に.” Learn the verb and its relationship to each phrase.

cards.title: Waiting for a length of time

blocks.text: **十分 / じゅっぷん — ten minutes; 三十分 / さんじゅっぷん — thirty minutes**, course model readings. じっぷん is also a standard variant of 十分; do not mark it linguistically wrong. This course uses じゅっぷん consistently for practice.
**十分待ちます。** じゅっぷん まちます。 — I wait for ten minutes.
**午前十時まで待ちます。** ごぜんじゅうじまで まちます。 — I wait until 10 AM.
The first says how long; the second gives an endpoint. 十分 read じゅうぶん means sufficient in another word, an unscored preview; context selects our minute word.

cards.title: Invite a companion: ませんか

blocks.text: For a simple invitation, use the familiar polite stem＋**ませんか**. This asks the other person's inclination rather than only denying an action.
**いっしょに行きませんか。** いっしょに いきませんか。 — Would you like to go together?
**いっしょに休みませんか。** いっしょに やすみませんか。 — Shall we take a rest together?

いっしょに means together. Invitation context matters: an ordinary negative question can have other uses. The course tests an explicit “invite your companion” situation, not an ambiguous sentence with no context.
Replace ます with **ましょう** to propose a shared action or agree to an invitation.
**行きましょう。** いきましょう。 — Let's go.
**休みましょう。** やすみましょう。 — Let's rest.
**待ちましょう。** まちましょう。 — Let's wait.

ましょう can sound more directive than asking ませんか. Use it after shared agreement in our dialogue. It is not a te-form and does not require learning 待って yet. We are extending polite stems already learned.
**午後一時に南口で会います。** ごごいちじに みなみぐちで あいます。 — We meet at the south exit at 1 PM.
**友だちはまだです。** ともだちは まだです。 — My friend has not arrived yet / is not here yet, in this meeting context.
**十分待ちましょう。** じゅっぷん まちましょう。 — Let's wait for ten minutes.

まだです is the previously taught short reply. The general “has not done it yet” construction will be introduced in Kusatsu after te-form instruction; do not substitute まだ来ません as a universal perfect-tense translation.
**A: いっしょに店に行きませんか。** いっしょに みせに いきませんか。 — Would you like to go to the shop together?
**B: はい、行きましょう。** はい、いきましょう。 — Yes, let's go.
**A: 午後二時に行きます。** ごごにじに いきます。 — We will go at 2 PM.
**B: ここで待ちます。** ここで まちます。 — I will wait here.
The invitation asks, the answer agrees, and the schedule names the time. Polite words help us coordinate, while the factual location and time remain fictional.

items: Read 鹿嶋, 立つ, 待つ. **Answers:** かしま; たつ; まつ.
Which radical is on 待's left? **Answer:** 彳, ぎょうにんべん.
Complete “wait for my friend”: 友だち＿＿待ちます。 **Answer:** を.
Invite someone to rest together. **Model:** いっしょに休みませんか。
Agree to wait. **Model:** はい、待ちましょう。
Why are 鹿嶋市 and 鹿島神宮 spelled differently? **Answer:** They are separate official proper-name spellings; preserve each.

blocks.text: 鹿嶋 is the city; 鹿島神宮 is the shrine name. 立つ→立ちます and 待つ→待ちます share the つ-to-ち polite-stem change. 待 has 彳, not 亻. Wait for someone with を, at a place with で, for a duration without time-point に in our model. ませんか invites; ましょう proposes/agrees.
**Recall:** “Would you like to go together?” → “Yes, let's go.” **Model:** いっしょに行きませんか。はい、行きましょう。 いっしょに いきませんか。はい、いきましょう。 Next: making things in 笠間.
